sections: Routine nutrient observations: original visits and censor bounds

This section uses the original 2023 SWS-2023 routine nutrient cohort at SV-268 and SV-374: 96 reported results in 24 source activities, with 12 visits at each station. Twenty-four total-nitrogen values combine Kjeldahl nitrogen and nitrate plus nitrite within the same source activity, date, fraction, project and sample clock. Ammonia remains part of Kjeldahl nitrogen and is not added again. The 120 calculated value rows comprise those 96 original results and 24 within-activity sums.

Each reported below-limit result retains a conservative nonnegative concentration enclosure and its original strict relation. Mean lower and upper endpoints use every selected visit and the same denominator; no half-limit value or zero-valued measurement is substituted. These enclosures describe retained measurement limits, rather than statistical confidence intervals.

sections.caption: All original routine visits; the station date sets differ. Full-precision values, activity identities and original source rows accompany the report.

sections: The routine nutrient cohort and the separate special-study chlorophyll campaign retain their own dates, depths and programme identities. Their counts are presented separately throughout the source tables.
Routine nutrient contrasts within observed flow bands

The complete 365-day approved record at upstream gauge USGS 02186702 defines discharge quartile boundaries of 30.6, 53.9 and 75.3 ft³/s. Q1 includes values at or below the first boundary; Q2 and Q3 exclude their lower boundary and include their upper boundary; Q4 contains values above 75.3 ft³/s. Each original routine visit is assigned its same-calendar-day gauge mean.

sections.caption: Descriptive, unmatched visit groups with two to five visits per station/band. Flow bands retain the actual gauge-day context; they do not establish matching water parcels or hydraulic travel time.

sections: The phosphorus and within-activity total-nitrogen mean enclosures remain separated between these stations in all four observed-flow bands. Interpreting transport, retention or annual nutrient load requires the relevant outlet geometry, concentration coverage and flow-weighting method.
Same-date routine measurements and the June 12 event

May 17 is the sole calendar date shared by the two routine station cohorts. The original SV-268 activity began 13:39 EDT and SV-374 began 11:32 EDT; the upstream gauge daily mean was 64.7 ft³/s. The table retains this timing difference.

sections.caption: 2023-05-17 source activities AF02075 and AF02069; full original activity prefixes and source-result IDs are retained in same_date.csv.

sections: The June 12 SV-268 activity AF03778 coincided with a 604 ft³/s gauge daily mean, at the 99.315th midrank percentile of the year's daily values. Its constituent contrasts are calculated against the other 11 routine visits at that station, all below the annual gauge 95th percentile.

sections.caption: Constituents respond differently: event phosphorus was 0.180 mg/L, while within-activity total nitrogen was 0.660 mg/L. Comparison dates, source activities and original strict bounds travel with june12_contrast.csv.
